text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prosecutor's office investigates the killing of four supporters of the Democratic Party in 1991.
- Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, on his first visit to Albania, met President Sali Berisha and other senior officials.
- Recent opposition protest in Belgrade has also divided the Albanian authorities and leaders of ethnic Albanians in Kosovo.
- Thousands of people eager to retrieve their deposits surrounded the office of a collapsed pyramid scheme company Sude.
- Japan's Toyota opens a servicing plant in Albania.
- Athens mayor Dimitris Avrompoulos, on a visit to the Albanian capital, discussed extending cooperation with the Tirana city hall and senior officials.
- Lushnja soccer club bought Argentinian Matio Kempes, the well-known World Cup 1978 winner, as its new coach for $300,000.
- Astrit Hafizi, national soccer team coach, will look for new players to make up the team after its recent loss.
